claim: Chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) are synthetic receptors that reprogram T cells to kill cancer.
source: Chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) are synthetic receptors that reprogram T cells to kill cancer.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about CAR technology.

claim: CAR-T cell therapies have been successful, highlighting the promise of programmed immunity.
source: The success of CAR-T cell therapies highlights the promise of programmed immunity and suggests that applying CAR strategies to other immune cell lineages may be beneficial.
evidence: Referenced as an established success in the abstract.

claim: CAR-Ps consist of an extracellular antibody fragment that can be modified to direct CAR-P activity towards specific antigens.
source: CAR-Ps consist of an extracellular antibody fragment, which can be modified to direct CAR-P activity towards specific antigens.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract describing the structure of CAR-Ps.

claim: The cytosolic domains from Megf10 and FcRɣ robustly triggered engulfment independently of their native extracellular domain.
source: By screening a panel of engulfment receptor intracellular domains, we found that the cytosolic domains from Megf10 and FcRɣ robustly triggered engulfment independently of their native extracellular domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: CAR-Ps drive specific engulfment of antigen-coated synthetic particles.
source: We show that CAR-Ps drive specific engulfment of antigen-coated synthetic particles and whole human cancer cells.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: CAR-Ps drive specific engulfment of whole human cancer cells.
source: We show that CAR-Ps drive specific engulfment of antigen-coated synthetic particles and whole human cancer cells.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated in Figure 4.

claim: Addition of a tandem PI3K recruitment domain increased cancer cell engulfment.
source: Addition of a tandem PI3K recruitment domain increased cancer cell engulfment.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by data in Figure 4e.

claim: CAR-P expressing murine macrophages reduce cancer cell number in co-culture by over 40%.
source: Finally, we show that CAR-P expressing murine macrophages reduce cancer cell number in co-culture by over 40%.
evidence: Stated in abstract and supported by data in Figure 4f.

claim: CAR-T cells recognizing CD19 have been used successfully to target hematological malignancies with 70–90% of patients showing measurable improvement.
source: CAR-T cells recognizing CD19, a marker expressed at high levels on the surface of B cells and B cell-derived malignancies, have been used successfully to target hematological malignancies with 70–90% of patients showing measurable improvement (Lim et al., 2017; Engel et al., 1995; Haso et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: CD19 is a marker expressed at high levels on the surface of B cells and B cell-derived malignancies.
source: CAR-T cells recognizing CD19, a marker expressed at high levels on the surface of B cells and B cell-derived malignancies, have been used successfully to target hematological malignancies with 70–90% of patients showing measurable improvement (Lim et al., 2017; Engel et al., 1995; Haso et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Macrophages are critical effectors of the innate immune system, responsible for engulfing debris and pathogens.
source: Macrophages are critical effectors of the innate immune system, responsible for engulfing debris and pathogens.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about macrophage function.

claim: Macrophages are uniquely capable of penetrating solid tumors, while other immune cells, like T cells, are physically excluded or inactivated.
source: Macrophages are uniquely capable of penetrating solid tumors, while other immune cells, like T cells, are physically excluded or inactivated (Lim et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Early efforts transferring healthy macrophages into cancer patients failed to inhibit tumor growth.
source: Early efforts transferring healthy macrophages into cancer patients failed to inhibit tumor growth, suggesting that macrophages require additional signals to direct their activity towards tumors (Lacerna et al., 1988; Andreesen et al., 1990).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Macrophages require additional signals to direct their activity towards tumors.
source: Early efforts transferring healthy macrophages into cancer patients failed to inhibit tumor growth, suggesting that macrophages require additional signals to direct their activity towards tumors (Lacerna et al., 1988; Andreesen et al., 1990).
evidence: Inferred from cited studies showing failure of macrophage transfer.

claim: Antibody blockade of CD47 reduced tumor burden.
source: Antibody blockade of CD47, a negative regulator of phagocytosis, reduced tumor burden, indicating that shifting the balance in favor of macrophage activation and engulfment is a promising therapeutic avenue (Majeti et al., 2009; Chao et al., 2010; Jaiswal et al., 2009; Tseng et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: CD47 is a negative regulator of phagocytosis.
source: Antibody blockade of CD47, a negative regulator of phagocytosis, reduced tumor burden, indicating that shifting the balance in favor of macrophage activation and engulfment is a promising therapeutic avenue (Majeti et al., 2009; Chao et al., 2010; Jaiswal et al., 2009; Tseng et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Macrophages expressing CAR-PMegf10 or CAR-PFcRɣ promoted significant engulfment of CD19 beads compared to macrophages with no CAR.
source: Macrophages expressing a CAR-P with the Megf10 (CAR-PMegf10) or FcRɣ (CAR-PFcRɣ) intracellular domain promoted significant engulfment of CD19 beads compared to macrophages with no CAR (Figure 1b,c, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data shown in Figure 1b,c.

claim: Macrophages expressing CAR-PBai1, CAR-PMerTK, and the adhesion-only CAR-PGFP did not bind the CD19 beads.
source: Macrophages expressing CAR-PBai1, CAR-PMerTK, and the adhesion-only CAR-PGFP did not bind the CD19 beads even though these CAR-Ps are present at the cell surface (Figure 1b,c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 1b,c and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: CAR-PBai1, CAR-PMerTK, and CAR-PGFP are present at the cell surface.
source: Macrophages expressing CAR-PBai1, CAR-PMerTK, and the adhesion-only CAR-PGFP did not bind the CD19 beads even though these CAR-Ps are present at the cell surface (Figure 1b,c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in text and demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Primary murine bone marrow derived macrophages expressing CAR-PFcRɣ were able to trigger engulfment of CD19 beads.
source: To confirm that the CAR-P was a viable strategy for redirecting primary macrophages, we expressed the CAR-PFcRɣ in primary murine bone marrow derived macrophages and found that these transfected primary cells also were able to trigger engulfment of CD19 beads (Figure 1d).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 1d.

claim: ɑCD22 CAR-PMegf10 promoted engulfment of CD22 beads.
source: Consistent with our results using ɑCD19-based CARs, ɑCD22 CAR-PMegf10 promoted engulfment of CD22 beads (Figure 2a).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 2a.

claim: CD19 beads were not eaten by ɑCD22 CAR-PMegf10 macrophages.
source: CD19 beads were not eaten by ɑCD22 CAR-PMegf10 macrophages, and CD22 beads were not eaten by ɑCD19 CAR-PMegf10 macrophages (Figure 2a).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 2a.

claim: CD22 beads were not eaten by ɑCD19 CAR-PMegf10 macrophages.
source: CD19 beads were not eaten by ɑCD22 CAR-PMegf10 macrophages, and CD22 beads were not eaten by ɑCD19 CAR-PMegf10 macrophages (Figure 2a).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 2a.

claim: CAR-PMegf10 specifically triggers engulfment in response to the target ligand.
source: These data indicate that CAR-PMegf10 specifically triggers engulfment in response to the target ligand and that the CAR-P strategy is able to target multiple cancer antigens.
evidence: Inferred from the specificity data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The CAR-P strategy is able to target multiple cancer antigens.
source: These data indicate that CAR-PMegf10 specifically triggers engulfment in response to the target ligand and that the CAR-P strategy is able to target multiple cancer antigens.
evidence: Inferred from successful targeting of both CD19 and CD22.

claim: CAR-PMegf10 was able to trigger specific engulfment of beads ranging from 2.5 µm to 20 µm in diameter.
source: We found that CAR-PMegf10 was able to trigger specific engulfment of beads ranging from 2.5 µm to 20 µm in diameter, with higher specificity above background engulfment being demonstrated for the larger beads (Figure 2b).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: Higher specificity above background engulfment was demonstrated for larger beads.
source: We found that CAR-PMegf10 was able to trigger specific engulfment of beads ranging from 2.5 µm to 20 µm in diameter, with higher specificity above background engulfment being demonstrated for the larger beads (Figure 2b).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: CAR-PMegf10 macrophages engulfed CD19 beads and beads containing 10% phosphatidylserine and ICAM-1 at a similar frequency.
source: We found that CAR-PMegf10 macrophages engulfed CD19 beads and beads containing 10% phosphatidylserine and the adhesion molecule ICAM-1 at a similar frequency (Figure 2b).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 2b.

claim: The CAR-P is comparably efficient to the endogenous system.
source: This indicates that the CAR-P is comparably efficient to the endogenous system.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of CAR-P engulfment with endogenous Megf10 ligand engulfment.

claim: Macrophages expressing CAR-PMegf10 exhibited an increase in phosphotyrosine at the synapse.
source: Macrophages expressing CAR-PMegf10 exhibited an increase in phosphotyrosine at the synapse, while macrophages expressing CAR-PGFP did not show this enrichment (Figure 3a).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 3a.

claim: Macrophages expressing CAR-PGFP did not show phosphotyrosine enrichment at the synapse.
source: Macrophages expressing CAR-PMegf10 exhibited an increase in phosphotyrosine at the synapse, while macrophages expressing CAR-PGFP did not show this enrichment (Figure 3a).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 3a.

claim: CAR-PMegf10 initiates engulfment through a localized signaling cascade involving tyrosine phosphorylation.
source: This result suggests that CAR-PMegf10 initiates engulfment through a localized signaling cascade involving tyrosine phosphorylation.
evidence: Inferred from phosphotyrosine enrichment data.

claim: F-actin was enriched at the cell bead synapse.
source: Consistent with previous reports, we found that F-actin also was enriched at the cell bead synapse (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both successful CAR-P intracellular domains (from FcRɣ and Megf10) have cytosolic Immunoreceptor Tyrosine-based Activation Motifs (ITAMs).
source: Both successful CAR-P intracellular domains (from FcRɣ and Megf10) have cytosolic Immunoreceptor Tyrosine-based Activation Motifs (ITAMs) that are phosphorylated by Src family kinases.
evidence: Stated as a structural feature of the successful CAR-P domains.

claim: ITAMs in FcRɣ and Megf10 are phosphorylated by Src family kinases.
source: Both successful CAR-P intracellular domains (from FcRɣ and Megf10) have cytosolic Immunoreceptor Tyrosine-based Activation Motifs (ITAMs) that are phosphorylated by Src family kinases.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about ITAM phosphorylation.

claim: The CD3ζ subunit of the T cell receptor contains three ITAM motifs.
source: The CD3ζ subunit of the T cell receptor contains three ITAM motifs.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about CD3ζ structure.

claim: The CAR-T was able to trigger engulfment of CD19 beads to a comparable extent as CAR-PMegf10.
source: The CAR-T was able to trigger engulfment of CD19 beads to a comparable extent as CAR-PMegf10 (Figure 3c).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 3c.

claim: In T cells, phosphorylated ITAMs in CD3ζ bind to tandem SH2 domains (tSH2) in the kinase ZAP70.
source: In T cells, phosphorylated ITAMs in CD3ζ bind to tandem SH2 domains (tSH2) in the kinase ZAP70.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about T cell signaling.

claim: Zap70 is not expressed in macrophages.
source: Zap70 is not expressed in macrophages, but Syk, a phagocytic signaling effector and tSH2 domain containing protein, is expressed at high levels (Andreu et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Syk is a phagocytic signaling effector and tSH2 domain containing protein expressed at high levels in macrophages.
source: Zap70 is not expressed in macrophages, but Syk, a phagocytic signaling effector and tSH2 domain containing protein, is expressed at high levels (Andreu et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Syk kinase can bind to the CD3ζ ITAMs.
source: Previous work suggested that Syk kinase can also bind to the CD3ζ ITAMs (Bu et al., 1995), indicating that the CAR-T may promote engulfment through a similar mechanism as CAR-PFcRɣ.
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Syk-tSH2 binds CD3ζ with an affinity of approximately 15 nM.
source: Our results show that Syk-tSH2 binds the CD3ζ and FcRɣ with comparable affinity (~15 nM and ~30 nM respectively, Figure 3d).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 3d.

claim: Syk-tSH2 binds FcRɣ with an affinity of approximately 30 nM.
source: Our results show that Syk-tSH2 binds the CD3ζ and FcRɣ with comparable affinity (~15 nM and ~30 nM respectively, Figure 3d).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 3d.

claim: The TCR CD3ζ chain can promote phagocytosis in a CAR-P, likely through the recruitment of Syk kinase.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that the TCR CD3ζ chain can promote phagocytosis in a CAR-P, likely through the recruitment of Syk kinase.
evidence: Inferred from binding affinity data and engulfment results.

claim: 78% of CAR-PMegf10 macrophages internalized bites within 90 min.
source: Strikingly, the majority of CAR-P-expressing macrophages internalized bites of the target cell (Figure 4a, Figure 4—video 1, 78% of CAR-PMegf10 and 85% of CAR-PFcRɣ macrophages internalized bites within 90 min).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4a.

claim: 85% of CAR-PFcRɣ macrophages internalized bites within 90 min.
source: Strikingly, the majority of CAR-P-expressing macrophages internalized bites of the target cell (Figure 4a, Figure 4—video 1, 78% of CAR-PMegf10 and 85% of CAR-PFcRɣ macrophages internalized bites within 90 min).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4a.

claim: The biting phenotype resembles trogocytosis, or nibbling of live cells.
source: The biting phenotype resembles trogocytosis, or nibbling of live cells, which has been reported previously in immune cells (Joly and Hudrisier, 2003).
evidence: Stated with citation to previous work.

claim: Trogocytosis has been reported previously in immune cells.
source: The biting phenotype resembles trogocytosis, or nibbling of live cells, which has been reported previously in immune cells (Joly and Hudrisier, 2003).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Removing the signaling domain (CAR-PGFP) dramatically reduced trogocytosis.
source: This process was dependent on the ITAM-bearing intracellular signaling domain, as removing the signaling domain (CAR-PGFP) dramatically reduced trogocytosis (Figure 4a).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4a.

claim: Enrichment of phosphotyrosine at the cell-cell synapse supports active signaling initiating trogocytosis.
source: Enrichment of phosphotyrosine at the cell-cell synapse further supports active signaling initiating trogocytosis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The CAR-P module was able to induce trogocytosis in non-professional phagocytes, human NIH 3T3 fibroblast cells.
source: The CAR-P module also was able to induce trogocytosis in non-professional phagocytes, human NIH 3T3 fibroblast cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The CAR-P can promote cancer antigen-dependent engulfment by both professional and non-professional phagocytes.
source: This suggests that the CAR-P can promote cancer antigen-dependent engulfment by both professional and non-professional phagocytes.
evidence: Inferred from successful trogocytosis in both macrophages and fibroblasts.

claim: Macrophages expressing CAR-PMegf10 or CAR-PFcRɣ were capable of engulfing whole Raji B cells (2 cancer cells eaten per 100 macrophages in a 4–8 hr window).
source: We observed that macrophages expressing the CAR-PMegf10 or CAR-PFcRɣ were capable of engulfing whole Raji B cells (2 cancer cells eaten per 100 macrophages in a 4–8 hr window for both CAR-PMegf10 or CAR-PFcRɣ, Figure 4b,e, Figure 4—video 2).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4b,e.

claim: Blockade of CD47 using the mouse IgG1 anti-human B6H12 clone resulted in a 2.5 fold increase of whole cell eating of opsonized Raji B cells.
source: While addition of this antibody did not trigger additional whole cell internalization, blockade of the 'don't eat me' signal CD47 using the mouse IgG1 anti-human B6H12 clone resulted in a 2.5 fold increase of whole cell eating of opsonized Raji B cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: PI3K signaling is important for internalization of large targets.
source: Previous work demonstrated that PI3K signaling is important for internalization of large targets (Schlam et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: A CAR-P containing the p85 recruitment motif alone (CAR-PPI3K) was able to induce some whole cell engulfment, comparable to the CAR-PFcRɣ.
source: A CAR-P containing the p85 recruitment motif alone (CAR-PPI3K) was able to induce some whole cell engulfment, comparable to the CAR-PFcRɣ (Figure 4e).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4e.

claim: Expression of CAR-Ptandem tripled the ability of macrophages to ingest whole cells compared to CAR-PGFP (6 cancer cells eaten per 100 macrophages).
source: Expression of CAR-Ptandem tripled the ability of macrophages to ingest whole cells compared to CAR-PGFP (6 cancer cells eaten per 100 macrophages, Figure 4d,e, Figure 4—video 3).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4d,e.

claim: Assembling an array of motifs designed to recruit distinct phagocytic effectors can increase CAR-P activity towards whole cells.
source: These data indicate that assembling an array of motifs designed to recruit distinct phagocytic effectors can increase CAR-P activity towards whole cells.
evidence: Inferred from the improved performance of CAR-Ptandem.

claim: After 44 hr of co-culture, CAR-P macrophages significantly reduced the number of Raji cells.
source: After 44 hr of co-culture, we found that CAR-P macrophages significantly reduced the number of Raji cells (Figure 4f).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4f.

claim: The CAR-PFcRɣ performed nearly as well as CAR-Ptandem at eliminating Rajis.
source: Although the CAR-Ptandem was much more efficient at whole cell eating, the CAR-PFcRɣ performed nearly as well at eliminating Rajis.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of data in Figure 4f.

claim: The CAR-P is a successful strategy for directing macrophages towards cancer targets.
source: Overall, these data suggest that the CAR-P is a successful strategy for directing macrophages towards cancer targets, and can initiate whole cell eating and trogocytosis leading to cancer cell elimination.
evidence: Inferred from all experimental results showing engulfment and cancer cell reduction.

claim: CAR-P can initiate whole cell eating and trogocytosis leading to cancer cell elimination.
source: Overall, these data suggest that the CAR-P is a successful strategy for directing macrophages towards cancer targets, and can initiate whole cell eating and trogocytosis leading to cancer cell elimination.
evidence: Directly stated as a summary of experimental findings.

claim: Spatial segregation between Src-family kinases and an inhibitory phosphatase, driven by receptor ligation, is sufficient to trigger signaling by the T cell receptor.
source: Previous work has suggested that spatial segregation between Src-family kinases and an inhibitory phosphatase, driven by receptor ligation, is sufficient to trigger signaling by the T cell receptor (Davis and van der Merwe, 2006; James and Vale, 2012) and FcR (Freeman et al., 2016).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Spatial segregation between Src-family kinases and an inhibitory phosphatase, driven by receptor ligation, is sufficient to trigger signaling by FcR.
source: Previous work has suggested that spatial segregation between Src-family kinases and an inhibitory phosphatase, driven by receptor ligation, is sufficient to trigger signaling by the T cell receptor (Davis and van der Merwe, 2006; James and Vale, 2012) and FcR (Freeman et al., 2016).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: The CAR-Ps may convert receptor-ligand binding into receptor phosphorylation of ITAM domains through partitioning of kinases and phosphatases at the membrane-membrane interface.
source: The CAR-Ps that we have developed may similarly convert receptor-ligand binding into receptor phosphorylation of ITAM domains through partitioning of kinases and phosphatases at the membrane-membrane interface.
evidence: Speculative inference based on cited mechanisms.

claim: Targeting of tumor cells by macrophages has been suggested to cause tumor cell killing.
source: Targeting of tumor cells by macrophages has been suggested to cause tumor cell killing (Jaiswal et al., 2009; Majeti et al., 2009; Chao et al., 2010; Jadus et al., 1996), either through directly engulfing cancer cells or by stimulating antigen presentation and a T cell-mediated response (Liu et al., 2015; Tseng et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Macrophages can kill tumor cells either through directly engulfing cancer cells or by stimulating antigen presentation and a T cell-mediated response.
source: Targeting of tumor cells by macrophages has been suggested to cause tumor cell killing (Jaiswal et al., 2009; Majeti et al., 2009; Chao et al., 2010; Jadus et al., 1996), either through directly engulfing cancer cells or by stimulating antigen presentation and a T cell-mediated response (Liu et al., 2015; Tseng et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Inhibition of the CD47-SIRPA 'Don't eat me' signaling pathway has been shown to result in engulfment of cancer cells.
source: Inhibition of the CD47-SIRPA 'Don't eat me' signaling pathway has also been shown to result in engulfment of cancer cells (Chen et al., 2017; Gardai et al., 2005; Jaiswal et al., 2009; Majeti et al., 2009; Chao et al., 2010).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: CD47 inhibition is most effective when combined with a positive signal to promote target engulfment.
source: A recent study suggests that CD47 inhibition is most effective when combined with a positive signal to promote target engulfment, which raises the possibility of combining CAR-P expression with CD47 or SIRPA inhibition for an additive effect (Alvey et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: The engulfment of larger 20 micron beads was more frequent than the engulfment of whole cells.
source: Although we were able to increase whole cell engulfment by recruiting the activating subunit of PI3K to the phagocytic synapse, the engulfment of larger 20 micron beads was more frequent than the engulfment of whole cells.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of data in Figures 2b and 4e.

claim: Differing physical properties of the engulfment target may explain differences in engulfment frequency between beads and cells.
source: We hypothesize that this is due to differing physical properties of the engulfment target.
evidence: Speculative explanation for observed differences.

claim: Increased target stiffness has been shown to promote engulfment.
source: Specifically, increased target stiffness has been shown to promote engulfment, suggesting that manipulating the physical properties of the engulfment target could also be a potential strategy for increasing CAR-P efficiency (Beningo and Wang, 2002; Cross et al., 2007).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Trogocytosis has been described in immune cells.
source: Trogocytosis, or nibbling of living cells, has also been described in immune cells (Harshyne et al., 2003; Harshyne et al., 2001; Kao et al., 2006; Joly and Hudrisier, 2003; Batista et al., 2001) and brain-eating amoebae (Ralston et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Trogocytosis has been described in brain-eating amoebae.
source: Trogocytosis, or nibbling of living cells, has also been described in immune cells (Harshyne et al., 2003; Harshyne et al., 2001; Kao et al., 2006; Joly and Hudrisier, 2003; Batista et al., 2001) and brain-eating amoebae (Ralston et al., 2014).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: Endogenous dendritic cell populations ingest bites of live tumor cells, contributing to presentation of cancer neo-antigen.
source: In vivo studies also have shown that endogenous dendritic cell populations ingest bites of live tumor cells, contributing to presentation of cancer neo-antigen (Harshyne et al., 2001; Harshyne et al., 2003).
evidence: Cited from published literature.

claim: The authors were not able to detect robust cross presentation of the model antigen ovalbumin using CAR-P in dendritic cells.
source: Although we were able to use the CAR-P to induce trogocytosis in dendritic cells, we were not able to detect robust cross presentation of the model antigen ovalbumin (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Directly stated and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Using CAR-Ps to enhance cross presentation of cancer antigen would likely require more optimization of the dendritic cell subset employed or the CAR-P receptor itself.
source: Thus, although using CAR-Ps to enhance cross presentation of cancer antigen is an intriguing future avenue, such a strategy would likely require more optimization of the dendritic cell subset employed or the CAR-P receptor itself.
evidence: Speculative statement about future directions based on negative results.

claim: The CAR approach is transferrable to biological processes beyond T cell activation.
source: Overall, our study demonstrates that the CAR approach is transferrable to biological processes beyond T cell activation and that the expression of an engineered receptor in phagocytic cells is sufficient to promote specific engulfment and elimination of cancer cells.
evidence: Inferred from successful application of CAR strategy to phagocytosis.

claim: The expression of an engineered receptor in phagocytic cells is sufficient to promote specific engulfment and elimination of cancer cells.
source: Overall, our study demonstrates that the CAR approach is transferrable to biological processes beyond T cell activation and that the expression of an engineered receptor in phagocytic cells is sufficient to promote specific engulfment and elimination of cancer cells.
evidence: Directly stated as a summary conclusion supported by all experimental data.
